title: P5.1 (HIGH): Empirical-prior data leakage in utils/empirical_priors.py
description: utils/empirical_priors.py computes priors from finisher data that is also fed to the likelihood, violating Bayesian principles. Fix: add explicit train/prior split — hold out 20% of races for prior elicitation, fit model on remaining 80%. Document split in data_processing.py. Alternative (cheaper): use weakly-informative priors from ultramarathon literature.

title: nb 2 needs convergence at (3, 629) — refit on faster hardware
description: Notebook 2 was switched to numpyro on macOS (nutpie has a numba cumsum-axis bug with LKJCholeskyCov). On Apple Silicon CPU, numpyro takes >50 min for tune=500/draws=500 and didn't finish in the overnight session. Old cached (3, 629) trace had r_hat=1.01 but came from a stale data snapshot (48 courses vs current 43), so cells like urSm/cEAS/VCRE error on dimension mismatch. Fix: fit fresh on RunPod/GPU or accept smaller k-core like (3, 800) for dev iteration.

title: nb 4 (unobserved DNFs) needs full work — cached trace at (3, 840) is unidentifiable r_hat~4.5

Cached (3, 840) trace shows r_hat=2.94-4.57 across all hyperparameters, sigma_obs huge, mu_logit_dnf=157 (unrealistic). Needs: (a) check observed_times unit consistency like nb 1, (b) likely larger k-core for identifiability, (c) consider hierarchy simplification per UltraSignup-6rg. Did NOT start in overnight session due to time budget.

title: P3.5: last_scraped_at unreliable for 52K races (results inserted without timestamp update)
description: Validation surfaced that ~52,435 races have last_scraped_at IS NULL but DO have results in the results table. The scraper inserts results without updating races.last_scraped_at. Affects the 'find races without results' optimization in scrape-results which uses last_scraped_at to filter. Fix: in database/operations.py, ensure results inserts also set races.last_scraped_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP for the parent race, OR change the 'find races without results' query to use EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM results) instead of last_scraped_at IS NULL. Surface visible in analysis/notebooks/data_validation.py section 5.

title: P3.2-followup: distance parser should prioritize suffix-after-last-dash
description: Parser scans left-to-right and returns first match. Multi-distance race names like 'Mt Shasta 50m/50k/30k/10k - 30K' return 50K (first match) instead of 30K (the actual race per the trailing convention). Affected: at least 60 races with leading distance lists. Fix: in DistanceExtractor.extract_distance, if race name contains ' - ', try extraction on the substring after the last ' - ' first; fall back to full-name scan only if suffix yields None. Verify with the backfill script (scraper/scripts/backfill_distances.py).
close_reason: Implemented suffix-after-last-dash priority in DistanceExtractor.extract_distance. Backfill applied: 2,810 races with corrected distances. Fix and backfill in commit on scraper main branch.

title: P2.2-followup: scrape-races-incremental --since-date should be optional per README
description: The README at scraper/README.md (around line 110-115) documents 'scrape-races-incremental --max-workers 6' as a valid usage with auto-detected start date. But the click @main.command decorator at scraper/main.py:357 declares --since-date as required=True, so the documented usage actually errors. The dead-code duplicate that we removed in P2.2 (UltraSignup-7co) had this option marked as optional with help 'defaults to last scrape timestamp', suggesting that was the intended behavior. Make --since-date optional and verify run_scrape_races_incremental_mode handles since_date=None (probably uses races.last_scraped_at to auto-detect).
close_reason: Removed required=True from --since-date click option; mode function already handled None correctly. Help text updated to document fallback chain (last scrape timestamp -> 30 days ago).

title: P5.4: Censoring penalty approximation in notebook 4
description: Penalty -n_finishers[c]*log(E[P(finish)]) uses an expectation; bias depends on individual predictions. Replace with exact marginal likelihood (integrate P(finish|x_i) over observed finishers) or use posterior-predictive simulation to estimate bias.

title: P5.3: Hierarchy identifiability in notebook 4
description: Three-level hierarchy (population to course to race) risks sigma_race collapsing to zero. Fit simpler 2-level version (no race level) and compare via LOO-IC using arviz.compare. Inspect posterior widths on sigma_race; if data does not support it, drop the race level.

title: P5.2: Likelihood mismatch on finish times (notebooks 1, 2, 4)
description: Notebook 1 puts Normal noise on log-pace then exponentiates; notebook 2 uses LogNormal with sigma fixed at 0.15. Change to a proper LogNormal likelihood with sigma as a learned parameter (HalfNormal(0.3) prior is reasonable). For notebook 4, allow sigma to vary by gender or by course size.
notes: Unit-bug part of this is fixed in commit c75b3cc — observed_times now in minutes consistent with expected_time. Likelihood is still Normal-on-time (not strict LogNormal), but with corrected units the sigma scales sensibly (~2 min finish_time_noise) and r_hat=1.02. Strict LogNormal would still be cleaner — leaving open.

title: P3.2: Fix distance_km parsing bug (5K/10K/Half races mis-parsed as ultras)
description: The earlier '1931-03-31 race_date' concern turned out to be a non-issue (single virtual entry; pre-1990 historical races like JFK 50 from 1963 are legitimate). The real parsing bug is in distance_km: at least 1247 short races (named '5K', '10K', 'Half Marathon') were parsed as ultra distances because the parser pulled numbers from suffix tokens in the race name. Worst example: 'Run For Your Life 5k & 800m Kids Run' got distance_km=1287.475 (= 800 miles, parsed from '800m'). Files to investigate: scraper/ultrasignup_scraper/core/distance_extractor.py and scraper/ultrasignup_scraper/parsing/races.py. Need to: (1) fix the regex/parsing logic, (2) re-extract distances for affected races (likely via backfill SQL or scraper command).
close_reason: Fixed root cause: distance_extractor matched lowercase 'm' as miles. Backfilled 65 races. The original 1931-03-31 concern was a non-issue. Suffix-priority for multi-distance names tracked as UltraSignup-a3d.
